producer_report.summary:
The producer loop now scans its own work for added email addresses outside the allow-list. A finding is sent back once, naming file:line, and fails the run if it is still there. Introspection now finds earlier cases of a repeated admission refusal, whatever their class of work.

**Producer loop (root cause 1: no in-loop scan).**
- `athena_gate::content` gains `added_email_lines` and `email_lines_in_changes`. A line counts as added only if the base has no identical line left to match it. Deleted files, gitlinks and binary blobs are skipped.
- `producer_loop` runs the scan after every report, using the same allow-list and `disallowed_emails` rule as admission.
- Findings join the existing single send-back, through the new `send_back_text_with_emails` (`send_back_text` is now test-only).
- If a finding is still there after the send-back, the run fails with "email scan refused the change: README.md:3 adds an email address outside the allow-list". No checks or verifier run. The address itself never appears in the reason, the UI lines or the send-back text.
- `admission.rs` now publishes its fixed refusal wording once, as `EMAIL_REFUSAL`, `REFUSAL_PHRASES` and `refusal_kinds`. Its messages are built from those constants, so the text is unchanged. It also adds `email_refusal_at(path, line)`.

**Introspection (root cause 2: `narrow_cases`/`apply_answer` did not match the admission refusal reason).**
- `OutcomeRow` reads the outcome's `reason`, and `Records.job_reasons` keeps every outcome reason of each job.
- `narrow_cases` still matches on class of work and category. It now also keeps a case whose job reasons share a refusal kind with the new event's text.
- Doc comments on `narrow_cases` and `apply_answer` name the cause.
- This covers the seven fixed-wording refusals in `REFUSAL_PHRASES`, not only email. Secret findings, governance and configuration messages have variable text and are not matched.

**Other changes.**
- One new line in `producer.md`: "Identities (names, emails) come from config or git settings, never from literals in code."
- A `CHANGELOG.md` entry names both root causes.
- Tests are in `admission.rs` (including `the_in_loop_email_scan_flags_only_what_admission_flags` for the "no stricter than admission" claim), `athena-gate` content tests, `run/tests.rs`, `athena-cap-change` and `athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs`.
- With the scan and the matcher clause temporarily disabled, the criterion 1 test and both criterion 3 tests failed. I restored both afterwards.

checks_run.note: Ran with a filter on `email_lines`; it matched two of the new unit tests. Both pass.
15 tests pass, including the subset test and the refusal-kinds test.
38 tests pass, including the two new run-loop tests.
Both new introspection tests pass. They fail when the matcher clause is disabled.
Passes with the new producer.md line and no edit to docs/system-facts.md.
12 tests pass. The boundary scan found no banned word or fragment.
The whole-workspace run exited 0. The output was too large to read back, so I judged the result from the exit status.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-core: a new test gives the producer a working diff adding a disallowed email on a known line of a known file and asserts the run fails with a message naming that file and line; it fails on base code and passes with the change.
criteria_check.evidence: Test: `a_producer_that_adds_a_disallowed_email_is_sent_back_once_then_fails_naming_file_and_line` in run/tests.rs. It passes. It asserts the job is Failed, the reason contains README.md:3 and the admission phrase, there are two producer runs and no verifier run, the second prompt names README.md:3, and the address appears nowhere. With the scan call temporarily emptied, it failed with 'admission refused the change: README.md adds an email address outside the allow-list', which has no line number.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-core: a test with an allow-listed address, or none, in the working diff asserts the producer run is not failed by the new scan. An address already present in the base is not blamed.
criteria_check.evidence: `the_email_scan_leaves_allow_listed_and_pre_existing_addresses_alone` in run/tests.rs passes. Both jobs reach Landed with one producer run and no 'sent back' line: one adds an allow-listed address, the other keeps a disallowed address the base already holds. Unit tests `added_email_lines_number_only_the_lines_the_old_text_lacks` and `email_lines_in_changes_skips_deleted_files_gitlinks_and_binary_blobs` in athena-gate cover no address, allow-listed, unchanged, moved and duplicated lines, deleted files, gitlinks and binary blobs. `the_in_loop_email_scan_flags_only_what_admission_flags` shows the in-loop scan flags nothing admission does not.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-core: a new introspect test builds records where two earlier jobs' outcomes record 'adds an email address outside the allow-list', and asserts the narrowed earlier-case list for a new event with that refusal includes both. It also asserts the resulting introspection record has non-empty earlier_cases and new_class is false. It fails on base code.
criteria_check.evidence: The two tests are in crates/athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs, so I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli --test introspection admission_refusal`, not the athena-core command. Both pass. `earlier_cases_by_admission_refusal_are_found_across_classes_of_work` builds `job_reasons` for two jobs and asserts `narrow_cases` returns both, newest first, plus controls and a second kind (size). `a_repeat_admission_refusal_in_another_class_of_work_is_not_a_new_class` runs three real failing jobs of classes docs, config and other. It asserts the second record's earlier_cases is the first record's id, and the third lists both earlier ids, has new_class false, and the registry holds one class. With the matcher clause disabled, the unit test failed with an empty list.

criteria_check.criterion: Code comments or commit text name both root causes: no in-loop scan, and narrow_cases/apply_answer not matching on the admission refusal reason. CHANGELOG.md has an entry.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test; all pass.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. All three exited 0.

criteria_check.criterion: The change refuses more producer runs than before by design: expected 5% of newly refused readings; the higher rate is intended because it moves the existing admission email refusal earlier and adds no new rule.
criteria_check.evidence: The in-loop scan uses admission's own `disallowed_emails` rule and allow-list and counts only lines the base lacks. `the_in_loop_email_scan_flags_only_what_admission_flags` shows its flagged paths are a subset of admission's for the allow-listed, unchanged-line, moved, duplicated and deleted forms, and equal for a plain new address. That test also asserts admission's message is unchanged and the in-loop message is the path:line form of the shared constant. The 5% figure is an estimate I did not measure.

open_issues: The plan expected a docs/system-facts.md edit. The budgets test already passes, so I made none. The brief's 146 tokens left and the doc's 1257 of 1300 do not agree. I did not investigate which is right.

Gitleaks secret findings and the governance and configuration messages have variable wording. A repeat of those refusals is still matched only by class of work and category, as before. Extending the matcher needs those messages split into a fixed phrase and variable parts.
A model that answers 'new' despite matching cases listed in its prompt still creates a class. `apply_answer`'s logic is unchanged; whether code should override that is for the maintainer.
On the in-loop email failure the producer's work tree is not kept, as on the 'no valid report' path. I did not settle whether to keep it the way `keep_timed_out_work` does.
I ran the full workspace test once, as allowed. The saved output was too large to read back, so I judged it from the exit status, which was success.
mistakes: My first end-to-end introspection test used the `code` and `design` classes, which the reader refuses without extra assumptions. I switched to docs, config and other.
I first wrote the third record's earlier_cases assertion in oldest-first order. The list is newest first, so I corrected it.
learnings: `DiffEntry` (athena-git) has `old_mode`, `new_mode`, `old_oid`, `new_oid`, `status` and `path`. `Snapshot::change_list()` diffs the base against the work tree, and `Snapshot::blob(oid)` reads a blob from the snapshot's own repository.
`GateError` converts from `GitError` and is `std::error::Error`, so `?` carries it into anyhow in the producer loop.
Introspection reads outcomes with `read_records(root)` from the working tree. A case's `job` is `Option<String>`, which is the key into `job_reasons`.

The reader refuses a `code` or `design` class reading in tests unless it carries `Code survey:` or `Existing code:` assumptions. Tests that need different classes of work can use docs, config and other.
`narrow_cases` returns cases newest first, so a model asked to list earlier cases gets and returns them in that order.
A blanket `cargo test --locked` shows a failure as `Exit code 101`. A silent success is the only way to tell the whole workspace passed when the output is saved to a file the tools cannot read.
docs/system-facts.md's producer budget figure did not change with the one-line prompt addition.
desires: A way to read a saved large tool-output file from inside the working directory, to confirm per-binary test counts for the full run.
